page: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an entry-level virtual server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware architecture supplies 1 physical core mapped to 1 dedicated vCPU without simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory is configured at 4.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio. Fast local storage is bundled via a 30 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Performance metrics indicate reliable single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core reaching 3035.28 and Geekbench single-core scoring 1813.0. Single-threaded compression throughput shows stable mid-range results, posting 28.4 GB/sec in gzip. Because execution is confined to a single physical core, multi-threaded output mirrors single-threaded figures, resulting in low aggregate multi-core scores in Geekbench and PassMark CPU evaluations. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 31.44 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 22.58 GB/sec for writes, which places overall memory throughput and static web delivery in the lower percentiles relative to multi-core configurations.

By delivering dedicated CPU hardware rather than burstable or shared thread models, the instance provides predictable computational consistency. The combination of dedicated processing, 4.0 GB of memory, and fast NVMe storage fits small microservices, CI/CD worker nodes, low-traffic API endpoints, staging environments, and single-threaded background tasks that require isolated core resources.
description: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an entry-tier server in the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup, offering 1 dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC CPU core running at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of memory, and 30 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Its dedicated single-thread architecture eliminates noisy-neighbor contention common in burstable tiers, delivering stable single-core compute verified by a stress-ng score of 3035.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1813.0. Because total throughput is bound by a single physical core, multi-core and aggregate database operations reflect lower benchmark tiers, complemented by modest uncached memory read bandwidth of 31.44 GB/sec. Featuring a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM profile with local NVMe performance, this configuration provides consistent processing capacity for lightweight microservices, small API routers, CI/CD worker agents, and dedicated development environments.
